value.body:
Scope from Jack Heart: reorg plus the top-level docs pass, using the reduce skill. His words: "I do want to take the reorg and docs class and see if we can throw in there using the reduce skill in Flow and thinking like: Okay we've accumulated a lot of code for what should be a relatively small system due to a lot of iteration on how we think about what it is, what parts to focus on, and how they interrelate. Hopefully we should be able to, by reorganizing the system, make it clear what parts we really need. As we go through them we ask, \"Okay where does this really belong? But also do we actually still need this?\"" Starts after #117 lands.
Approach: (1) reduce over the whole package first (src/etude, about 34k lines, 106 modules): what the product is, mismatches, and per module "where does it belong" and "do we still need it", written to scratch/simplification-opportunities.md; (2) the layout by level follows from that, deleting what is not needed in the same change (git keeps it; no shims unless released records require readers); (3) the eval vocabulary and seed model already on this Task; (4) the docs pass for the reader who builds with Etude: one-screen README, docs/getting-started.md quick start, a guide for going further with quirks, a limits page, internals moved to docs/dev/, each doc opening with its purpose and reader and covering only that (Jack Heart: "making sure that each doc has a clear purpose, is speaking to that specific thing, and isn't getting bogged down in the complexities of how the system interrelates"). Full docs brief: "Top-level docs" section of the EXP-73 checkout's scratch/exp-73-group-an-experiment.md. Before 0.4.1. No release.
